flow_transcript_slices.question: Tell me about yourself and why early childhood education matters to you.
flow_transcript_slices.candidate_transcript:
[Q1 Attempt 1]
A little bit about myself is I used to work in human resources. I recently left that this past year. I started working at Small World Preschool, so it's going to be my first year finishing up as a teacher. And I chose early childhood education because that was something that sparked my interest. I wanted to work with kids, and I knew I wanted to be a teacher when I started going to school. Yes. Yes, I did.

flow_transcript_slices.question: Why are you applying for this position, specifically at Launch Pad Learning?
flow_transcript_slices.candidate_transcript:
[Q2 Attempt 1]
I feel like having the experience as a preschool teacher, I feel like it allows me to bring my expertise to your company.

flow_transcript_slices.question: Tell me about a time a child was having a really hard moment emotionally. What did you notice about what they were feeling, and how did you respond?
flow_transcript_slices.candidate_transcript:
[Q3 Attempt 1]
I had this one incident with a child where they just had a total miscommunication of emotions. They were yelling, screaming. They were kind of having a hard time breathing. I noticed they got really red, and it was just too much emotion for them at once. I helped them by talking to them, doing some breathing exercises, and just assuring them that at school they're safe, there's no need to worry about anything, and that they're just in a safe environment with other children.

flow_transcript_slices.question: Tell me about a time you felt overwhelmed at work with children present. What did you do to manage yourself?
flow_transcript_slices.candidate_transcript:
[Q4 Attempt 1]
At work, I usually don't get stressed around children, but I do like to take some time to myself during my 10-minute breaks or my lunch just to de-stress and decompose by coloring or just reading.

flow_transcript_slices.question: Imagine you’re caring for a child who clearly does not want to be touched during a routine task, like diapering, helping with clothing, or guiding them physically. They are pulling away or saying no. Walk me through exactly what you would do, step by step
flow_transcript_slices.candidate_transcript:
[Q5 Attempt 1]
So if a child doesn't want to be touched, I would go down to their eye level and start asking them how they're feeling and assuring them that it's okay, it's the transition time, or if they need to be changed, it's time for them to get changed. I'm also doing a reward system where, hey, come on and let's go get you changed, or let's go do this transition, and you'll get a sticker, or just making transition time, or anything that needs to get done, having it to be fun for them, rather than like a chore or a task. If that didn't work, I would try to call my team for help. If not... It escalated to that further.

flow_transcript_slices.question: Tell me about a time you received feedback you didn’t expect or didn’t fully agree with. What happened next?
flow_transcript_slices.candidate_transcript:
[Q6 Attempt 1]
Well, we were having an issue with scheduling just because some kids get hungrier earlier in the day and sometimes when we do circle time, some kids say they're hungry and they're not really paying attention because they're hungry or they want to go outside and play. We would just switch up the schedule and see what works for each children. Everybody was receptive of the feedback of changing the schedule because I pay attention to them. Over the schedule change, I received positive feedback. I haven't received any negative feedback over the schedule change. No.

flow_transcript_slices.question: Can you share something you’ve learned about children or yourself over time that changed how you approach your work?
flow_transcript_slices.candidate_transcript:
[Q9 Attempt 1]
My approach to work for myself, being a first-year teacher, I felt that working with children helped me grow more, learning to have more patience and just knowing how to do things more fun with children, getting them interacting with each other.

flow_transcript_slices.question: Tell me about a time a child’s behavior was challenging for you. How did you approach it?
flow_transcript_slices.candidate_transcript:
[Q10 Attempt 1]
During one of our Christmas shows, we had one of the children just completely scream and crying, throw themselves on the floor. What I did is just I took that child to the side and then I tried to comfort them the best way I could by ensuring them, you know, their parents were in the crowd, that it's okay to be scared, and just assure them that they're safe with their teacher.
